edits.walkthrough_append: **EXAM TRAP:** Growth kinetics follow LAG → LOG (exponential, straight line on semi-log paper) → STATIONARY (nutrient/space limits) → DEATH — the SPECIFIC growth rate µ is measurable only in LOG phase, and MONOD kinetics ties µ to substrate concentration; reading doubling time off the stationary phase, or treating lag as growth, loses the kinetics marks.

**EXAM TRAP:** Entrez links one QUERY across databases — Gene → nucleotide → protein → PubMed → structure — with ACCESSION numbers as the cross-database keys; and BLAST (sequence similarity) is a different tool from Entrez (database retrieval), though results link between them; treating Entrez as a sequence-alignment program confuses retrieval with search-by-sequence.

**EXAM TRAP:** Octal digits run 0-7 ONLY — the digit 8 in an octal number is invalid on sight — and decimal-to-octal uses repeated DIVISION by 8 with remainders read BOTTOM-UP; writing remainders top-down (or including an 8 in an octal literal) are the two standard conversion errors.

**EXAM TRAP:** The BASE fixes the digit SET (0 to base−1) AND each position's value (base^position) — a valid number cannot contain a digit equal to or above its base; and converting BETWEEN bases via decimal (base-n → decimal → base-m) is the safe two-step when a direct rule is not memorised.

**EXAM TRAP:** Floating point stores SIGN, EXPONENT, MANTISSA — many decimals (0.1) are NOT exactly representable in binary, so comparisons like 0.1 + 0.2 == 0.3 fail — and a bigger exponent range trades precision away; testing equality of floating-point values instead of comparing within a tolerance is the classic programmer's slip.

**EXAM TRAP:** Single precision = 32 bits split 1-8-23 (≈7 significant digits); double = 64 bits split 1-11-52 (≈15-16 digits) — the EXPONENT field grows, not the sign; and mixing the two in one expression PROMOTES to double automatically — quoting 1-11-23 for single, or forgetting the promotion, loses the precision-comparison mark.

**EXAM TRAP:** ASCII uses 7 bits (128 codes) with an 8th bit historically for parity — uppercase and lowercase codes differ by exactly 32, which is why case conversion is arithmetic; and ASCII covers ENGLISH only — Unicode (superset) assigns code points to every script, so claiming ASCII encodes Hindi characters is the standard misstatement.

**EXAM TRAP:** A truth table lists ALL 2ⁿ input combinations for n variables — missing a row (or listing 2n rows) breaks completeness — and the output column must follow the CONNECTOR'S definition row by row; evaluating intuitively instead of row-wise is exactly the shortcut the table exists to prevent.

**EXAM TRAP:** A formula is VALID (tautology) when EVERY row is true, CONTRADICTION when every row is false, CONTINGENT otherwise — one false row disqualifies validity — and proving validity requires the full table or a derivation, not intuition; calling a contingent statement valid because it "looks true" is the standard misjudgement.

**EXAM TRAP:** NAND and NOR are UNIVERSAL gates — any circuit, including NOT/AND/OR, can be built from either — and De Morgan's laws (¬(A·B) = ¬A + ¬B) convert between forms; simplifying with De Morgan requires DISTRIBUTING the negation over both inputs — dropping a negation inside the bracket is the standard algebra slip.

**EXAM TRAP:** The booking scenario's KEY question is what can go WRONG concurrently — two users booking the last seat — which is why verification-before-update and transactions matter; and every input (age, quota, date) needs validation BEFORE the state changes; answering with UI design alone misses the concurrent-access reasoning the scenario is built to test.

**EXAM TRAP:** An exception is an OBJECT thrown at runtime carrying state and behaviour — uncaught, it terminates the thread after unwinding — checked exceptions must be handled or declared, unchecked (RuntimeException) need not; catching Exception to swallow errors silently, or treating exceptions as compile-time issues, loses the mechanism marks.

**EXAM TRAP:** A withdrawal method must VALIDATE before MUTATING — throw IllegalArgumentException (or a custom exception) when balance is insufficient, leaving the balance UNCHANGED — catching the exception inside the same method and printing a message instead of throwing hides the failure from the caller, the design flaw the banking scenario targets.

**EXAM TRAP:** The THROWS clause DECLARES checked exceptions a method may propagate — it does not throw them (throw does) — and the CALLER must then catch or re-declare; declaring unchecked exceptions is legal but meaningless, and adding throws to main just pushes the burden — mixing throw/throws vocabulary is the standard 2-mark trap.

**EXAM TRAP:** The FINALLY block runs WHETHER OR NOT an exception occurs — even after a return in try — its job is CLEANUP (close files, release connections); only System.exit() skips it, and putting a return inside finally silently swallows the try's return — the guaranteed-cleanup purpose, not "error handling", is what the question scores.

**EXAM TRAP:** Objects-first means students USE objects (create, call methods, observe behaviour) before writing class internals — the pedagogy trades syntax-first drills for early mental models; and objects bundle STATE + BEHAVIOUR — describing objects-first as "learning variables first" inverts the approach's defining order.

**EXAM TRAP:** An interface is a pure CONTRACT (no instance fields, abstract methods by default) letting one class fulfil MULTIPLE types — escaping Java's single-inheritance limit — and implementers must define EVERY method or declare themselves abstract; giving an interface instance variables, or claiming it replaces inheritance entirely, loses the contract semantics.

**EXAM TRAP:** Methods are invoked by MESSAGE PASSING — object.method(arguments) — and the signature (name + parameter list) decides which overload runs; RETURN type alone never distinguishes overloads, and instance methods implicitly receive this — calling a method "a variable that runs" or ignoring the signature rule loses the invocation-logic mark.

**EXAM TRAP:** A constructor has the SAME NAME as the class and NO return type (not even void) — it INITIALISES new objects and can CHAIN via this(...) — and the compiler supplies a no-arg default only when NO constructor is written; writing void before a constructor silently turns it into an ordinary method, the classic slip.

**EXAM TRAP:** A short is 16-bit SIGNED: range −32,768 to 32,767 — arithmetic overflow wraps silently (32,767 + 1 becomes negative), and a short in an expression is PROMOTED to int before arithmetic; assigning an int variable to short without an explicit cast is a compile error, not a warning.

**EXAM TRAP:** double gives ~15-16 SIGNIFICANT DIGITS, not decimal places after the point — 0.1 + 0.2 still prints 0.30000000000000004 — and monetary code should avoid binary floating point entirely (use BigDecimal or scale to paise); quoting 15 digits as "15 decimal places" misstates where the precision lives.

**EXAM TRAP:** A char is a 16-bit UNSIGNED Unicode code unit — it has no negative values — and char arithmetic works ('a' + 1 gives 'b' via its numeric code) — printing a char shows the character; assigning a negative literal or confusing the character '1' with the number 1 are the standard char-question traps.

**EXAM TRAP:** WIDENING (int → long → double) is automatic and lossless; NARROWING (double → int) needs an EXPLICIT cast and TRUNCATES toward zero — (int)9.9 gives 9, not 10 — and char-to-int widens while int-to-char needs a cast; assuming Java rounds on narrowing or auto-narrows in assignments loses the conversion mark.

**EXAM TRAP:** A variable's TYPE fixes what it can hold and which operations are legal — Java is STATICALLY typed, so type errors surface at COMPILE time — and local variables must be INITIALISED before use (no defaults, unlike fields); calling undeclared/uninitialised variables safe, or expecting runtime type flexibility like Python, misreads the language contract.

**EXAM TRAP:** Operator PRECEDENCE decides grouping; ASSOCIATIVITY (left-to-right for arithmetic, right-to-left for assignment) decides ties — 2 + 3 * 4 is 14, and a = b = c assigns right-to-left — and SHORT-CIRCUIT operators (&&, ||) skip the right operand when the left decides; evaluating && without its short-circuit property changes program behaviour, not just style.

**EXAM TRAP:** Primitives HOLD values; object variables hold REFERENCES — assignment copies the reference, so two variables can point at ONE object and mutate it together — and == compares REFERENCES for objects (use equals for content); writing "assignment copies the object" is exactly the aliasing misconception the question targets.

**EXAM TRAP:** The ternary operator RETURNS A VALUE — condition ? valueIfTrue : valueIfFalse — so it must be used where a value is expected (assignment, argument), not as a statement replacement for if-else with side effects; nesting ternaries without brackets destroys readability, and forgetting both branches is a syntax error, not a default.

**EXAM TRAP:** switch cases need BREAK — fall-through executes every following case otherwise — and the switch variable takes byte/short/char/int/String/enum (not long, float, boolean); a default case handles unmatched values and needs no break if last — writing case ranges (case 1..5) or omitting break deliberately without stating fall-through loses the marks.

**EXAM TRAP:** SCOPE runs from declaration to the end of the enclosing BLOCK — a variable declared inside a loop or if dies at that block's closing brace — and shadowing (an inner variable hiding an outer one) is legal but confusing; using a loop variable after the loop, or re-declaring it inside, is the compile error the scope rule predicts.

**EXAM TRAP:** A method's SIGNATURE is name + parameter list — the return type does NOT distinguish overloads — and parameters are typed, ordered, and scope-limited to the method; calling with FEWER or wrongly-typed arguments fails compilation (no coercion across incompatible types), the strictness that makes reusable abstractions safe.

**EXAM TRAP:** Each Student OBJECT carries its OWN instance variables (own roll number, own marks) — static members would be SHARED by all — and instance methods read the object's own fields via implicit this; declaring per-student data as static makes every student share one roll number, the canonical OOP error the scenario tests.

**EXAM TRAP:** main's signature is EXACTLY public static void main(String[] args) — missing static (no object exists yet), wrong capitalisation, or (int argc) C-style parameters all compile-fail or fail to launch — and main can be overloaded but the JVM calls only the exact signature; treating any void method named main as an entry point loses the launch-logic mark.

**EXAM TRAP:** An array holds a FIXED number of SAME-TYPE elements with ZERO-BASED indexing — valid indices run 0 to length−1, and length is a FIELD (no brackets) — accessing index length throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException at RUNTIME; counting from 1, or resizing an array by assignment, are the standard slips the roll-number analogy pre-empts.

**EXAM TRAP:** Single-pass max/min initialises BOTH with the FIRST element (not 0 — negative arrays break that) and compares each subsequent element ONCE, giving O(n) without sorting; initialising max to zero fails on all-negative arrays, and two separate loops are correct but not single-pass — the initialisation choice is where the mark lives.

**EXAM TRAP:** Bubble sort SWAPS adjacent out-of-order pairs, largest "bubbling" to the end each pass — with n−1 passes and an early-exit optimisation when no swap occurs (best case O(n), worst O(n²)); comparing non-adjacent pairs is selection-sort logic, and forgetting the shrinking inner bound re-compares sorted elements — both lose the algorithm-tracing marks.

**EXAM TRAP:** Scanner SPLITS input into TOKENS on whitespace by default — nextInt() reads one token and LEAVES the newline in the buffer, so a following nextLine() returns an empty string; consuming the leftover newline (an extra nextLine) is the fix, and forgetting it is the single most common input-handling bug in school Java.

**EXAM TRAP:** File reading must CLOSE the stream (try-with-resources or finally) or the handle leaks — read line-by-line with BufferedReader, and handle FileNotFoundException/IOException as CHECKED exceptions the compiler forces you to plan for; writing the search loop without the checked-exception handling does not compile — the compiler, not style, enforces it.

**EXAM TRAP:** Every recursion needs a BASE CASE that terminates and a RECURSIVE STEP that moves TOWARD it — missing or unreachable base cases give StackOverflowError, not an infinite loop — and each call gets its OWN variables on the stack; tracing requires stacking the calls in order, which is exactly what the exam asks you to show.

**EXAM TRAP:** Recursion solves by SELF-SIMILARITY — factorial(n) = n × factorial(n−1) with factorial(0) = 1 — and the SUB-PROBLEM must shrink every call; two mutually-recursive calls without progress never terminate, and memoisation fixes recomputation (naive Fibonacci is exponential); writing the recurrence without its base case is the standard half-answer.

**EXAM TRAP:** Base conversion by recursion prints remainders ON RETURN (after the recursive call) so digits emerge most-significant first — dividing by the base moves toward the base case (n == 0); printing BEFORE the call reverses the digits, the ordering slip the base-conversion trace always catches.

**EXAM TRAP:** Systematic testing is REPEATABLE — fixed inputs, known expected outputs, edge cases (zero, negative, empty, maximum) — and a test that never fails proves nothing new; boundary values are where algorithms break (off-by-one in loops, empty arrays), and testing only the happy path is exactly what the "repeatable quality gate" definition excludes.

**EXAM TRAP:** The Java API supplies PRE-TESTED, documented classes through PACKAGES — import brings them into scope (java.util.Scanner, not "Scanner package") — and the API saves testing time but you must still READ the method signatures; writing your own sort while claiming to use the API, or importing classes that do not exist, misses the reuse-with-verification habit.

**EXAM TRAP:** Reverse domain naming (com.school.project) guarantees GLOBAL uniqueness because domains are already unique — the package name mirrors ownership, so collisions cannot occur between organisations; using single-word packages (mypackage) or the reserved java.* prefix for your own code are both wrong, the latter because the JVM trusts java.* as core classes.

**EXAM TRAP:** Phishing is defeated by VERIFICATION habits — inspect the actual sender domain (not the display name), hover before clicking links, refuse credential requests, check for HTTPS and spelling tells — and banks NEVER ask for PINs/OTPs by mail; replying to verify legitimacy, or clicking to "unsubscribe" from phishing, are the actions the scam counts on.

**EXAM TRAP:** The FSF's framework is COPYRIGHT-law based: copyleft (GPL) uses copyright to GUARANTEE freedom — source available, modify allowed, derivatives must stay free — distinct from public domain (no rights reserved) and from freeware (free PRICE, closed source); equating "free software" with "no cost" or "no copyright" is precisely the confusion the FSF's four freedoms clarify.

**EXAM TRAP:** Growth kinetics follow LAG → LOG (exponential, straight on semi-log paper) → STATIONARY → DEATH — the specific growth rate µ is defined only in LOG phase and MONOD kinetics ties µ to limiting substrate; reading doubling time off stationary phase or treating lag as growth loses the kinetics marks.
